The paper makes the broad claim that ExTernD is “to our knowledge the only ternary quantization that can provably reach any target accuracy,” but the proof shown only establishes its own convergence and adds only the narrower corollary that “No fixed number of ternary planes has this property.” The paper does not substantiate the stronger uniqueness claim against all ternary quantization families.

The paper explicitly claims ExTernD is 'the only ternary quantization that can provably reach any target accuracy' (Sec. 2) by contrasting it with fixed-plane-count methods, which ignores that methods like PTQTP can also increase their capacity parameter K to form a continuous-capacity family.
